title: Principled RL for Flow Matching Emerges from the Chunk-level Policy Optimization
claim: Optimizing at the chunk level, with temporal dynamics, gives clearly better structure, lighting and detail than step-level baselines.
layout: 3x4 image grid, prompt text above each row, method labels below columns
description: A 3-row by 4-column grid of generated images. Each row has a text prompt centered above it: dancing cartoon potatoes, an anime princess in white and gold, and a rainbow chibi kitten on a postcard. Columns are labeled in purple handwriting-style text at the bottom: FLUX, DanceGRPO, GCPO without Temporal Dynamics, and GCPO with Temporal Dynamics. Moving left to right, the images get richer. The FLUX column is plain and flat. The DanceGRPO column adds some detail. The GCPO columns show more refined structure, lighting and ornament. The rightmost column has the most detailed, atmospheric scenes, such as a windowed room, a veil and jewelry, and a textured postcard border. The eye goes first to the colorful images and then to the column labels.
caption: Compared to GRPO, Group Chunking Policy Optimization (GCPO) yields a significant improvement in image quality, particularly regarding structure, lighting, and fine-grained details, demonstrating the superiority of chunk-level policy optimization. Notably, Notably, the contrast between columns 3 and 4 underscores the importance of chunking with the inherent temporal dynamics of flow matching, which substantially elevates aesthetic style and structure of images. Additional details are provided in Section B.1.
abstract: Recent Progress in post-training flow matching for text-to-image (T2I) generation with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated strong potential. However, it is hindered by a critical limitation: inaccurate advantage attribution. In this work, we argue that aggregating consecutive steps into a coherent 'chunk' and shifting the policy optimization paradigm from GRPO's step level to the chunk level can effectively mitigate the negative impact of this issue. Building on this insight, we propose Group Chunking Policy Optimization (GCPO), the first chunk-level reinforcement learning approach for post-training flow matching. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCPO achieves superior performance on both standard T2I benchmarks and preference alignment, with up to 43% relative gains over GRPO, highlighting the promise of chunk-level policy optimization. The code is available on https://github.com/xingzhejun/GCPO.
